title: Best Children's Workshops and Classes in Singapore (2026 Guide for Ages 3-12)
excerpt: Singapore is a wonderland of enrichment for kids. From coding bootcamps to pottery workshops, music lessons to sports classes, the Lion City offers world-class learning experiences for children aged 3 to 12. Here's our curated guide to the very best workshops and classes across the island.
content:
Singapore parents are spoiled for choice when it comes to enrichment classes. But with so many options, how do you find the ones that are truly excellent, genuinely fun, and worth your Saturday morning? We've done the research and rounded up the best children's workshops and classes in Singapore across five key categories. Whether your child is a budding artist, a future coder, or a music prodigy, there's something here for them.

Art Classes for Creative Minds

Artgrain — Multiple Locations

Artgrain is one of Singapore's most respected names in children's art education, with branches in Orchard, Tampines, and East Coast. Their programs are designed for children as young as 3, using a step-by-step method that builds confidence through guided drawing and painting. The classes cover watercolor, acrylic, pastels, and mixed media — and the results are genuinely impressive. Kids typically produce a finished artwork to bring home after every session.

Ages: 3 to 16 years
Pricing: Around SGD$55-75 per session for weekly classes. Trial sessions available.
Links: Book an Artgrain trial class on Klook for exclusive first-timer discounts.

Parent Verdict: "My 7-year-old has been going to Artgrain for a year and her improvement is incredible. The teachers are patient and really know how to bring out each child's creativity." — Mei Ling, mum of two, Tampines

The Artground — Goodman Arts Centre

The Artground is less a class and more an immersive art experience. Located at Goodman Arts Centre, this dedicated children's art space changes its themed interactive exhibition every few months. They also run drop-in art workshops most weekends where kids can try their hand at everything from clay sculpting to tie-dye. The style is exploratory — there are no wrong answers, just pure creative fun.

Ages: 1 to 12 years (workshops typically for 3+).
Pricing: Entry to the play space is SGD$12-15 per child; weekend workshops are SGD$25-40 extra.
Bonus: Highly recommended for rainy-day activities as the entire space is air-conditioned.

Coding, STEM, and Tech Workshops

Saturday Kids — Bugis + Online

If you want your child to learn real coding skills in a fun, project-based environment, Saturday Kids is the gold standard. Their programs cover Scratch (ages 6-8), Python (ages 9-12), and even Minecraft modding. Classes are kept small (max 8 students per instructor) and every child builds something they can show off — a game, an animation, or a website — by the end of the course.

Ages: 6 to 14 years
Pricing: Holiday camps from SGD$280-400; weekly term classes around SGD$400-550 per term (10 sessions).
Pro tip: Holiday camps sell out fast — secure your Saturday Kids spot on Klook to avoid disappointment.

Young Engineers — Multiple Locations

Young Engineers uses LEGO bricks and K'Nex to teach STEM concepts like mechanics, physics, and engineering design. The classes are hands-on from minute one: kids build motorized models of vehicles, cranes, and robots while learning about gears, torque, and angles. It's the kind of learning that feels like pure play.

Ages: 3 to 12 years (different levels for different age groups)
Pricing: Around SGD$50-70 per session for weekly classes.
Locations: Bukit Timah, Tampines, Novena, and more.

Music Lessons for Little Maestros

Mandeville Music Centre — Tanglin

Mandeville Music Centre offers one of Singapore's most comprehensive children's music programs, including the popular Yamaha Junior Music Course for ages 4-6. The course introduces keyboard playing, singing, rhythm exercises, and ear training in a fun, group setting. For older children, one-on-one lessons in piano, violin, guitar, and drums are available.

Ages: 2.5 (music appreciation) to 18 (ABRSM exam prep)
Pricing: Group courses from SGD$45-60 per session; private lessons from SGD$80-150 per hour.
Location: Tanglin Shopping Centre — centrally located and easy to reach.

Jin Wu — Multiple Locations

Jin Wu is a homegrown brand known for its friendly, low-pressure approach to music. They specialize in group keyboard and ukulele classes for younger children, with a curriculum that emphasizes fun songs over formal theory. Parents love the affordable rates and the relaxed end-of-term performances.

Ages: 4 to 12 years
Pricing: Group classes from SGD$35-50 per session — one of the most budget-friendly music options in Singapore.

Sports and Movement Classes

My Gym — Multiple Locations

My Gym is a staple of Singapore's enrichment scene for good reason. Their structured but playful classes focus on gross motor skills, coordination, and confidence through gymnastics, obstacle courses, and games. The equipment is sized just right for little ones, and the teachers are energetic and encouraging. They offer trial classes so you can see if it's a fit.

Ages: 3 months (!) to 10 years
Pricing: From SGD$60-85 per session. Multi-session packages offer better value.
Locations: Bukit Timah, Tanglin, Tampines, and Novena.

Little Kickers — Fields Across Singapore

Saturday morning football is a rite of childhood in many parts of the world, and Little Kickers brings it to Singapore in a big way. Their age-appropriate soccer programs use fun games and activities to teach basic ball skills, teamwork, and sportsmanship. Classes are held at parks and sports fields across the island.

Ages: 18 months to 8 years
Pricing: Around SGD$40-55 per session.
Note: Most sessions are outdoors, so bring sun protection and water.

Cooking Workshops for Junior Chefs

Yummy-Kid — Telok Ayer

Yummy-Kid offers Singapore's most popular cooking classes for children aged 3-12. In a purpose-built kitchen studio, kids learn to make everything from pizzas and pasta to cupcakes and sushi. Classes are hands-on — children do 95% of the work themselves, with gentle guidance from the instructors. The best part? They eat what they make.

Ages: 3 to 12 years
Pricing: From SGD$55-80 per session, depending on the recipe.
Location: 137 Cecil Street, Telok Ayer. Look for Yummy-Kid cooking classes on Klook to find seasonal holiday workshop deals.

Kid-Approved Quote: "I made spaghetti carbonara ALL BY MYSELF! We cooked it at the class and then I ate it for dinner. It was yummy!" — Chloe, age 8

Practical Tips for Enrichment Classes in Singapore

1. Trial first: Most reputable centers offer trial classes or single-session drop-ins. Take advantage of these before committing to a full term.
2. Location matters: Singapore traffic can be brutal. Choose a class near home or the MRT to avoid weekend burnout.
3. Waitlists are real: The most popular classes (especially Saturday Kids and My Gym) have waitlists. Book 4-6 weeks in advance.
4. Holiday camps: School holidays are prime time for intensive workshops. Many centers offer week-long camps that combine multiple activities.

Whether your child wants to code a video game, paint a masterpiece, kick a soccer ball, or bake the perfect chocolate chip cookie, Singapore's enrichment scene has them covered. Happy learning!
author: Kids Activities Asia Team
